analysis.title: International Market Intelligence | Morning Briefing (Nov 1, 2026)
key_insights: APAC markets are rising on Nov 1 with rotation out of defensives into cyclicals. Brent is below $110 on reports that Trump is giving Iran diplomacy more time, and China held market support meetings (STAR50 +3.5%). Weekend AI headlines were net negative (capital raising, circular financing, legal issues).

Global hedge fund performance fell about 3.5% in October. JPM Positioning Intelligence does not call the de-risking capitulatory (risks remain: possible quant de-grossing, elevated US Tech flows and futures positioning), but expects alpha could rebound.

Drew notes SPX returns after US midterms average +5.4%, +11.4%, +12.5% and +14.7% over 3, 6, 9 and 12 months, with a 100% positive hit rate at 6, 9 and 12 months since 1990. A Democratic sweep could be mildly dollar-bearish.

Client color from the marketing trip: APAC clients are more bearish than US clients but less so than EU clients. Many APAC clients are up double digits on the year and lack incentive to re-engage until a clear trend emerges.

The US consumer is described as robust. The top 4 income quintiles hold 6% to 27% more inflation-adjusted cash than at YE2019 (nearly $8T nominal). Retail sales run about $723bn a month YTD2026 versus $505bn in 2019. Card delinquencies and charge-offs are normalizing to pre-COVID trends, not deteriorating.
Corporate health is described as strong. HY default rates are 2.7% versus a 3.2% long-term average, after about 20% of HY market cap was upgraded to IG in the post-COVID era.

By consumer sub-sector: airlines, cruise lines and hotels show robust demand. Autos and homebuilders are rate-sensitive, with parts and suppliers suggested as an alternative. Retailers face freight costs of 30-40% of total cost that have more than tripled YTD. Restaurants see trade-down within quick service as negative. Staples are seen as most at risk of margin compression and a likely source of funds.

AI infrastructure has absorbed more than $500B of debt YTD (IG over $350B, leveraged over $60B, structured and private credit about $100B+). The HY compute index is +372bps YTD. Hyperscaler all-in funding costs are up about 120bps. JPM sees credit becoming more discriminating on AI infra but no broader funding crisis.

AI-related CDS spreads have widened on technical selling and bank hedging of data center lending exposure, not on fundamentals. CDS trades above cash-bond spreads, which JPM sees as an opportunity for investors willing to sell protection. CRWV has converts outstanding and CDS at a slightly positive basis.

ORCL and SpaceX credit spreads widened significantly on reports each is seeking off-balance-sheet financing. MSFT, GOOGL and AMZN spreads have held up better. JPM IG TMT research expects growing debt supply may pressure spreads into 2027, and sees Nvidia as a transmission channel for financial stress because of its ties to GPU customers including CRWV.

JPM HY credit analyst Tom Egan sees CRWV as a financing challenge, not a solvency one. He projects last-12-month EBITDA rising from about $4.4B (June 2026) to $7.3B by YE2026 and nearly $20B by YE2027, with about $130B of contracted revenue commitments.

JPM views France contagion fears as exaggerated. France has a primary deficit of about 3%, debt/GDP of about 120% and below-potential growth. JPM puts the 180% debt/GDP threshold 10-15 years away. OATs discount debt/GDP above 150% and an implied deficit above 8% versus about 5% debated. JPM sees room for relief into year-end around the budget but no material reversal before the 2Q27 elections.
JPM says EU bank earnings trends are unchanged and dips of more than 15% versus the index should be bought. It sees the backdrop as attractive for call ratio spreads and call spreads.

Midterms view: federal AI regulation is unlikely because Trump would veto and Democrats cannot reach a two-thirds majority. A Democratic House could defund Middle East military efforts. Tariff policy is unlikely to change. Longer-dated bonds could see a bid if Democrats halt deficit spending.

Treasuries: before the Oct 22 rally, JPM saw a 10-year yield of 5.50% as more likely than 5.00%. The market prices a hike in Dec 2026 and two in FY27. Clients see upside risk to that pricing. The downside view (fewer hikes after a quick end to the US/Iran conflict) is low conviction.

AI/tech pushback points: semis revenue is driven by supply-chain price spikes that are unsustainable in a DCF; neocloud turmoil may spread and bankruptcy risk exists; software is unlikely to be a funding source, and security and infra software are consensus longs. JPM says the buy trigger needs a positioning flush, hyperscaler capex confirmation, semis earnings, tighter credit and positive seasonality, which points to early November.

Broadening: since the July 28 lows the SPX is +4.8% (through Oct 22), but more than half the index has fallen and 69% of stocks lag the SPX. The 10Y yield averaged 2.39% in the 2010s versus 3.14% so far this decade.

An everything rally (AI and ex-AI together) is possible short term but not longer term, where JPM expects tech to dominate once the market stabilizes. About 65% of SPX companies cited AI operational improvement in 26Q2 earnings but under 5% quantified it.

Cyclicals: client interest is in Financials (GSIBs, credit cards), with indifference on gold-tilted Materials. Aero/Def has a negative outlook on the risk of a military funding halt, with a lame-duck defense bill as an upside risk. To fund tech longs, clients cite shorts in consumer, healthcare, small caps and Europe.

Other assets: the dollar is seen range-bound after a likely local high. Gold trades inversely to the dollar. Credit is not seen as superior to equities. Clients agree with the JPM copper bull case tied to a China growth reboot. Silver is seen as part of the AI trade.

JPM Market Intelligence is tactically bullish on global equities, preferring US and Asia (Japan, South Korea, Taiwan) over Europe. It says broadening is clearer in the US than the EU, and EU broadening needs stable EGB spreads.

Positioning Intelligence: the US Tactical Positioning Monitor is at the 33rd percentile (Oct 29), retail sentiment at the 6th percentile, ETF flows positive (+1z), CTA positioning at the 44th percentile. The TMT-versus-defensives sentiment gap at the 6th percentile echoes prior Tech-led rebounds. EU positioning rebounded from the 5th to the 14th percentile. China/HK positioning is the most bearish of any region at the 5th percentile.

HFs flipped to buying biotech and medtech, with healthcare flows the strongest of any sector last month. Utilities rallied while HFs kept selling, leaving the group with the lowest net positioning of any major industry.

market_movers.rationale: JPM HY credit calls CRWV a financing challenge, not a solvency one. It projects LTM EBITDA of $7.3B by YE2026 and about $20B by YE2027, with about $130B of contracted revenue.
ORCL credit spreads widened significantly on reports of off-balance-sheet financing, and externally financed companies underperformed.
JPM likes long Brazil as a hedge on a potential structural policy shift at the second round of the presidential election, and as a diversifier against EM AI weakness.
JPM likes EM for greater exposure to potential market broadening.
Large-cap China internet is the short leg of the tactical long China Star 50 versus KWEB trade, because it is more exposed to Chinese consumers.

sector_views.rationale: Needs longs across inference infrastructure, semi cap, less-levered hyperscalers and AI-vulnerable software. Tech is expected to dominate once the market stabilizes.
Unlikely to be a funding source going forward, and security and infra software are consensus longs. AI-vulnerable application software is a needed long.
Earnings trend unchanged, and dips of more than 15% versus the index should be bought.
Client interest in GSIBs and credit cards. US banks have a strong November seasonal record and HFs are net long.
Seen as most at risk of margin compression and a likely source of funds.
Clients see a negative outlook given the potential for a Blue Wave to halt a military funding spike.
HFs kept selling despite the rally, leaving the lowest net positioning of any major industry.
Rate-sensitive with affordability issues, and listed among JPM's shorts in the challenged industries.

earnings_insights: 20% of SPX and 17% of SXXP report in the week of Nov 2.
Earnings calendar: Nov 2 AAPL, PLTR. Nov 3 ANET, APO, ALAB, ISP, RACE. Nov 4 QCOM, ARM, DDOG, APP, NOVOB, BMW. Nov 5 NET, LITE, DBK, RHM, Toyota, Sony. Nov 6 MRNA.
Only under 5% of SPX companies that cited AI operational improvement in 26Q2 earnings were able to quantify the impact (about 65% mentioned AI improvement).
JPM says European earnings fundamentals are good, and EU bank earnings trends are unchanged.
Recent airline, cruise and hotel earnings releases and management commentary confirmed that demand remains robust despite higher prices.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Down on reports that Trump is giving Iran diplomacy more time. Resumption of combat operations is the consensus, which JPM says implies negative risk/reward for crude.
Spending is robust and higher energy prices are not crowding out discretionary spending.
Corporate credit health is strong, even after about 20% of HY market cap was upgraded to IG.

macro_indicators.reading: hike in Dec 2026 and two hikes in FY27
macro_indicators.interpretation: Clients see upside risk to this pricing. Fewer hikes would require a quick end to the US/Iran conflict and falling oil, product, petrochemical and shipping costs.

macro_indicators.reading: no hikes in FY27, cuts in FY28 and FY29, 2% target in FY29
macro_indicators.interpretation: Many clients think the dots are not tied to high-probability outcomes, so market pricing is the baseline for equity investors.

macro_indicators.reading: 5.50% more likely than 5.00% (pre Oct 22 rally view)
macro_indicators.interpretation: The forecast predates the Oct 22 rally.

macro_indicators.reading: about 120% actual vs above 150% discounted by OATs
macro_indicators.interpretation: OATs price a worse fiscal path than fundamentals, and JPM sees room for relief into year-end.
A headwind, but JPM says the situation is a French idiosyncratic story, not a Sov Crisis 2.0.

macro_indicators.reading: about -3.5% October MTD (estimate after Friday); -2.6% MTD through Oct 29
macro_indicators.interpretation: The worst month in a while for HFs, with declines across all regions and strategies.
Narrow breadth: 69% of stocks lag the SPX.

trade_ideas.description: Tactically long China Star 50 (STAR50) versus China Internet (KWEB)
trade_ideas.rationale: Captures more innovative and AI-exposed China tech, while large-cap internet is more exposed to Chinese consumers.

trade_ideas.description: Tactically long Korea versus South East Asia (ASEA)
trade_ideas.rationale: Expresses the AI winners versus losers view.
Follows the global tech selloff in July and offers less volatile exposure to AI and Asia tech than Korea.
Potential structural policy shift at the second round of the presidential vote, plus diversification from EM AI weakness and resilience to geopolitical risk.

trade_ideas.description: Long EM (EEM) for exposure to broadening
trade_ideas.rationale: Continued global macro strength, AI capex tailwinds, scope for policy easing and political catalysts.

trade_ideas.description: Call ratio spreads and call spreads on EU banks, buying dips of more than 15% versus the index
trade_ideas.rationale: Earnings trend is unchanged and the backdrop is attractive for these structures.

trade_ideas.description: Keep MCX < UKX option hedge, and short France versus EU Domestics
trade_ideas.rationale: Clarity is needed on spending, pragmatism and ideology; the French trade is for politics and dislocation.

trade_ideas.description: Sell CDS protection on AI infrastructure names trading at positive basis, such as CRWV
trade_ideas.rationale: CDS spreads are above cash-bond spreads because of bank hedging and technical selling, not fundamentals.
trade_ideas.risk: Higher rates, growing debt supply, delivery delays and interconnected financing.

risk_factors: Possible quant de-grossing and elevated US Tech flows and futures positioning.
AI headlines on capital raising, circular financing and legal issues.
Growing AI debt issuance, higher borrowing costs and interconnected financing arrangements, with Nvidia as a stress transmission channel.
Concentration and correlated downside risk from circular financing and Nvidia credit support.
Middle East escalation after the US midterms.
Further EGB spread widening resembling 2011-12, with France as a focus.
Semis revenue driven by supply-chain price spikes that may not be sustainable.
Neocloud turmoil spreading, with bankruptcy risk.
Higher rates and inflation, with the market pricing a Dec 2026 hike and two in FY27.
Retail freight costs that have more than tripled YTD, and margin compression in Staples.
vol_and_positioning: Global HF net returns were down about 4% on a rolling 20-day basis. The global long-short spread was -2.2% MTD (Asia -1.5%, N. America -1.9%, EMEA -2.4%).
Prior -3z events in the 20-day long-short spread saw positive forward 20-day spreads in 6 of 7 cases (average +1%).
Momentum exposure is at more than 12-month lows (about 30% of its peak). Risks include potential quant de-grossing and elevated US Tech flows and futures positioning.

The US Tactical Positioning Monitor fell to the 33rd percentile on Oct 29, with a neutral 4-week change. Retail sentiment is at the 6th percentile, ETF flows +1z, CTA positioning at the 44th percentile in US equities.
The JPM Split Congress Pair (JPMSC26P) has rallied to 2-year highs. Financials ETFs saw the strongest inflows last week.

Social media sentiment on TMT and the TMT-Defensives spread are both at the 6th percentile, similar to prior episodes (late Mar 2026, Mar/Apr 2025, early Aug/Sep 2024, late Apr 2024, end Dec 2022), each followed by Tech-led rebounds.
EU positioning hit the 5th percentile and rebounded to the 14th. China/HK aggregate positioning is at the 5th percentile, the most bearish of any major region.
Option ideas: call ratio spreads and call spreads on EU banks. Option hedges: keep MCX < UKX and short France versus EU Domestics.
geopolitical: Reports that Trump is giving Iran diplomacy more time pushed Brent below $110. Resumption of combat operations is consensus.
Concerns about escalation in the Middle East after the US midterm elections.
If Democrats take the House, they could defund military efforts in the Middle East and force an off-ramp for Trump.
A near-term end to the US/Iran conflict would lower oil, refined product, petrochemical and shipping/insurance costs, which could mean fewer Fed hikes.
China held market support meetings, and STAR50 rose 3.5%.
US midterm elections on Nov 3. Tariff policy is unlikely to change given the President's latitude over foreign policy.

tension_points.bull_case: JPM sees hyperscalers as fundamentally well-positioned, capital still available, and AI CDS widening driven by technical hedging demand, not fundamentals. CRWV is seen as a financing challenge with EBITDA rising toward about $20B by YE27.
tension_points.bear_case: Leveraged GPU and data center developers face tighter financing, with growing debt supply, circular financing, higher borrowing costs and delivery delays. Nvidia is a stress transmission channel and CRWV has bankruptcy risk.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Delivery of compute capacity falling behind schedule, or rising rates forcing larger equity contributions and revised deal structures for leveraged GPU financing.

tension_points.bull_case: Prior -3z alpha drawdowns saw positive forward spreads in 6 of 7 cases, de-grossing has been widespread and Momentum exposure is about 30% of its peak.
tension_points.bear_case: The de-risking has not been capitulatory, with possible quant de-grossing, elevated US Tech flows and futures positioning, and Middle East escalation risk after the midterms.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Quant de-grossing or a Middle East escalation after the midterms.

tension_points.bull_case: JPM sees OATs pricing a debt/GDP above 150% versus about 120% actual, ECB backstops (TPI, OMT, PEPP flexibility) and room for relief into year-end around the budget.
tension_points.bear_case: The tape echoes the 2011-12 sovereign crisis, with wider EGB spreads and lower EUR and EU banks, and France runs a roughly 3% primary deficit.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Disorderly spread widening if the ECB backstop is not activated, since activation is conditional.

tension_points.bull_case: Top-quintile cash piles, retail sales at $723bn a month, and normalizing credit card delinquencies.
tension_points.bear_case: Retail freight costs have more than tripled, trade-down within quick service restaurants, and rate-sensitive autos and homebuilders face affordability issues.

theme_stances.key_argument: Equities typically rise after midterms, and a Democratic sweep could be mildly dollar-bearish.
Credit is becoming more discriminating on AI infra, but nothing points to a broader funding crisis.
theme_stances.evidence: nothing to suggest a broader funding crisis

theme_stances.key_argument: Concerns that France leads EU-wide distress are exaggerated, and it is a French idiosyncratic story.
